story: Beyond Whiteboarding: Creating Expert System Architecture Diagrams
text: These fail my litmus test, which is, "can a third-party look at the diagram and make sense of it without verbal explanation?" For a more formal approach to coherent diagrams and white boarding, I recommend the C4 model. It's conceptually simple and results in better system documentation than the free form method that's commonly used. [VIDEO]

story: Ask HN: Visualizing software designs, especially of large systems (if at all)?
text: Recently stumbled upon [C4 Model]( [VIDEO] ), which seemed very promising. It builds on the failure of adopton of UMLs, and aim to be practical and communicative.

If C4 is new to you too, I recommend their intro video: [VIDEO] . It feels like a very light ruleset over what we would do naturally when explaining a system to another engineer. That's great. Some of the ideas that stood out were: 1. Allow flexibility in the notation (shapes and color) as long as the abstractions are good. 2. When drawing arrows, make them unidirectional to show the main intent. 3. Hide details to express the main story (@ 27min in the video) 4. Don't just give names to components. Give short descriptions too. 5. Don't document the lowest levels. Code is better here.

I've looked at mermaid & planetuml before. structurizr is new to me and looks interesting. PlanetUML has the advantage of gitlab support, iirc -- allowing rendering of diagrams in README files. I'd like to see more options for that. edit: interestingly, the author of structurizr (Simon Brown) was recently linked in another HN thread. HN thread - [LINK] YT link - [VIDEO]
